title: Presidential advisor held UFO material from a 1963 Marshall Islands nuclear detonation
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Presidential advisor held UFO material from a 1963 Marshall Islands nuclear detonation, about 1963 at Marshall Islands, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: We've even interviewed a top presidential advisor at the end of his life who admitted to holding UFO material that came from a nuclear detonation in the Marshall Islands in late 1963.
Or take presidential adviser Harold Malgren who held pieces of a UFO in his hands that came down from a high alitude nuclear test [music] in the Marshall Islands, the Bluegill Triple Prime test.
tellings.difference: Names the test as Bluegill Triple Prime in 1962 rather than late 1963, and credits Gise.
tellings.link_reason: Same claim that presidential adviser Malmgren held UFO material from a Marshall Islands high-altitude nuclear test.

as_told.title: Malmgren held UFO material from a Marshall Islands nuclear test

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he interviewed Harold Malmgren, a top advisor to US presidents, near the end of his life. According to Michels, Malmgren said he held pieces of a UFO that came down after a high-altitude nuclear test in the Marshall Islands, Pacific islands where the US tested bombs; Michels places it in late 1963 in one telling and names the 1962 test called Bluegill Triple Prime in others, crediting a man named Lawrence Preston Gise. If true, it would mean a senior official handled material from an unknown craft.
